Title: Organisation hierarchy
Acceptance intent: A study can involve three organisations without merging their users, contracts or data permissions.

Title: Verified organisation onboarding
Acceptance intent: An unverified applicant can prepare an application but cannot authorise data access or approve studies.

Title: Tenant boundaries
Acceptance intent: Cross organisation searches, direct links, exports and background jobs all reject ungranted access.

Title: Programme configuration
Acceptance intent: Two programmes can apply different eligibility and funding rules to the same product.

Title: Cross organisation collaboration
Acceptance intent: Accepting a study invitation grants only the study permissions specified in the approved agreement.

Title: Accountability register
Acceptance intent: Removing the last accountable owner is blocked until an authorised successor accepts responsibility.

Title: Lifecycle management
Acceptance intent: Suspension blocks new activity while preserving authorised incident response and required evidence access.

Title: Delegated network administration
Acceptance intent: A country administrator cannot change another country's rules or weaken mandatory operator controls.

Title: Institutional ownership changes
Acceptance intent: Historical reports retain the original legal entity and show the effective transfer date.

Title: Demonstration environment
Acceptance intent: A demo administrator cannot connect a production dataset or issue a production evidence report.

Title: User invitations
Acceptance intent: An expired or already accepted invitation cannot create another membership.

Title: Authentication
Acceptance intent: Each accepted write and approval is attributable to one uniquely identified human or service principal.

Title: Multifactor authentication
Acceptance intent: A restricted dataset remains inaccessible after password only authentication.

Title: Enterprise federation
Acceptance intent: A federated identity cannot claim an organisation or administrator role using an untrusted attribute.

Title: Provisioning and deprovisioning
Acceptance intent: A directory removal revokes mapped memberships within the agreed revocation objective and creates an audit event.

Title: Account recovery
Acceptance intent: A recovery attempt cannot replace a privileged authentication factor through email access alone.

Title: Session management
Acceptance intent: A revoked session fails its next protected action within the specified revocation limit.

Title: Membership changes
Acceptance intent: A departing reviewer loses active access without losing attribution on signed historical decisions.

Title: Temporary access
Acceptance intent: Expired access is denied by both the user interface and the API without manual cleanup.

Title: Service identities
Acceptance intent: A service credential cannot perform a human clinical signoff or inherit its owner's unrelated privileges.

Title: User preferences
Acceptance intent: Changing a display name does not alter the verified signer identity on an issued report.

Title: Professional verification
Acceptance intent: Expired credentials block new restricted decisions while preserving historical decisions for review.

Title: Identity reconciliation
Acceptance intent: Two accounts cannot be merged in a way that removes an existing conflict of interest declaration.

Title: Access recertification
Acceptance intent: The review lists actual effective privileges and records retain, reduce or revoke decisions.

Title: Permission model
Acceptance intent: A user with an evaluator role cannot read an unassigned study merely because both share a country.

Title: Granular actions
Acceptance intent: Permission to view a result does not automatically permit downloading its underlying records.

Title: Independent approval
Acceptance intent: A developer attempting to approve its own product's final report receives a recorded denial.

Title: Privileged administration
Acceptance intent: An administrator can manage an account without opening that account's restricted study files.

Title: Exceptional access
Acceptance intent: The access session expires automatically and generates a reviewable record of every protected action.

Title: Permission inheritance
Acceptance intent: An explicit dataset restriction remains effective when a user receives a broader programme role.

Title: Uniform enforcement
Acceptance intent: A denied user's search counts and file previews do not disclose hidden objects.

Title: Access request workflow
Acceptance intent: Approval for one purpose cannot be reused for an unrelated study or training activity.

Title: Dual control
Acceptance intent: One actor cannot satisfy two required approval roles on the same action.

Title: Permission changes during work
Acceptance intent: A queued export is cancelled when its grant expires before delivery.

Title: Permission explanations
Acceptance intent: A support explanation identifies the missing grant and responsible approver rather than revealing protected data.

Title: Conflict aware assignment
Acceptance intent: A reviewer with a declared material conflict is excluded until an independent decision is recorded.

Title: Country profiles
Acceptance intent: A study records the exact country profile version used at each gate.

Title: Applicability assessment
Acceptance intent: No study becomes active with an unanswered mandatory applicability item.

Title: Rule provenance
Acceptance intent: A source change creates a review task rather than silently changing a previously approved study.

Title: Residency and transfer rules
Acceptance intent: An otherwise valid workspace request is blocked when its region conflicts with the dataset policy.

Title: Restriction precedence
Acceptance intent: A permissive programme template cannot override a stricter data use agreement.

Title: Local terminology and language
Acceptance intent: A measurement is not interpreted in a different unit because a user changes display language.

Title: Rule change impact
Acceptance intent: Affected owners receive an actionable list with suspend, remediate or retain decisions and reasons.

Title: Authority boundaries
Acceptance intent: An internal successful evaluation cannot populate a market authorisation field.

Title: Regulatory collaboration
Acceptance intent: Two authorities reviewing the same solution see only the evidence explicitly shared with each.

Title: Profile activation
Acceptance intent: Marketing cannot advertise an active clinical sandbox in a country whose profile is still draft.

Title: Problem statements
Acceptance intent: An opportunity cannot advance to funded evaluation without a defined decision and accountable institution.

Title: Calls for solutions
Acceptance intent: Applicants retain the call version under which they submitted.

Title: Applicant screening
Acceptance intent: Rejected applicants receive authorised reasons and an available reconsideration route.

Title: Portfolio prioritisation
Acceptance intent: A ranking can be reproduced from its inputs and declared weights.

Title: Budget and buyer identification
Acceptance intent: A study lacking an adoption buyer is explicitly labelled exploratory and excluded from adoption readiness claims.

Title: Feasibility review
Acceptance intent: A feasibility decision records unresolved gaps and their cost and schedule consequences.

Title: Demand aggregation
Acceptance intent: A shared call produces distinct country decision records rather than one universal approval.

Title: Pipeline management
Acceptance intent: A pipeline report separates incomplete applications from scientifically unsuccessful evaluations.

Title: Site registry
Acceptance intent: A study can filter suitable sites using verified capabilities and current availability.

Title: Qualification and renewal
Acceptance intent: An expired qualification blocks new study allocation until reviewed.

Title: Capacity planning
Acceptance intent: Two programme managers cannot unknowingly allocate the same unavailable clinical capacity.

Title: Local accountability
Acceptance intent: A live study cannot open a site without all required local accountable roles.

Title: Partner agreements
Acceptance intent: An agreement expiry is visible before a new study or renewal is approved.

Title: Expert matching
Acceptance intent: A match explains its eligibility and never reveals a private competing application.

Title: Site performance
Acceptance intent: Performance comparisons disclose case mix and data completeness limitations.

Title: Partner suspension
Acceptance intent: Affected studies receive a documented reassignment or safe closure plan.

Title: Community participation
Acceptance intent: Community feedback has an accountable response and can influence the approved protocol.

Title: Product identity
Acceptance intent: A solution cannot enter evaluation with an undefined intended population or user.

Title: Version identity
Acceptance intent: Changing a decision threshold creates a new evaluated configuration rather than overwriting the old one.

Title: Submission package
Acceptance intent: Submission validation identifies missing mandatory materials before scientific review begins.

Title: Claims register
Acceptance intent: A developer supplied claim remains visibly distinct from a sandbox finding.

Title: Regulatory status
Acceptance intent: An authorisation for one use and jurisdiction is not displayed as unrestricted global clearance.

Title: Deployment modes
Acceptance intent: A black box API submission identifies reproducibility and inspection limits before acceptance.

Title: Dependency disclosure
Acceptance intent: An undeclared external model provider prevents activation of a restricted data evaluation.

Title: Commercial readiness
Acceptance intent: A procurement reviewer can distinguish evaluation access from production licensing rights.

Title: Confidentiality controls
Acceptance intent: Publishing a public solution profile does not expose its proprietary model files.

Title: Withdrawal and recall
Acceptance intent: A withdrawn version is unavailable for new studies while its historical evidence remains traceable.

Title: Comparable profiles
Acceptance intent: Search results do not rank unlike clinical tasks by a single undifferentiated accuracy score.

Title: Ownership disputes
Acceptance intent: A disputed uploader cannot transfer or delete the challenged asset during a hold.

Title: Agreement register
Acceptance intent: A study gate evaluates the active signed agreement rather than an unsigned draft.

Title: Rights by activity
Acceptance intent: Permission to run inference does not authorise training or model weight redistribution.

Title: Evidence ownership
Acceptance intent: A report export checks the rights of all contributing assets.

Title: Term and expiry
Acceptance intent: An expired data licence blocks new runs even if a study remains administratively open.

Title: Subprocessors and providers
Acceptance intent: A new provider cannot receive study data before its approval becomes effective.

Title: Funding restrictions
Acceptance intent: A charge outside the award period is flagged before invoicing or drawdown.

Title: Independence terms
Acceptance intent: A payer cannot remove an unfavourable finding from the signed scientific record.

Title: Contract exceptions
Acceptance intent: A commercial discount does not modify clinical safety or data protection requirements.

Title: Signature integration
Acceptance intent: Replacing an agreement file invalidates its prior signature association.

Title: Liability allocation
Acceptance intent: Activation is blocked where a required responsibility or coverage obligation is unresolved.

Title: Configurable gates
Acceptance intent: Users cannot skip an applicable ethics or data gate by changing a display status.

Title: Task orchestration
Acceptance intent: A blocked task shows the dependency and accountable party rather than an unexplained delay.

Title: Decision records
Acceptance intent: A report can reconstruct precisely which documents supported the decision.

Title: Parallel review
Acceptance intent: A blinded reviewer cannot see another review before its permitted unblinding point.

Title: Conditional decisions
Acceptance intent: An unmet prerequisite condition prevents the dependent activity from starting.

Title: Rework and resubmission
Acceptance intent: Reviewers can compare the changed material and distinguish new evidence from unchanged claims.

Title: Appeals
Acceptance intent: The original decision maker cannot be the sole adjudicator of the appeal.

Title: Suspension and resumption
Acceptance intent: A commercial manager cannot resume a clinical suspension independently.

Title: Amendments
Acceptance intent: An added site cannot recruit under another site's approval unless explicitly covered.

Title: Service clocks
Acceptance intent: Turnaround reporting cannot improve by silently resetting an application's start date.

Title: Ethics applicability
Acceptance intent: An evaluator cannot self declare exemption without the required institutional authority.

Title: Approval records
Acceptance intent: A study cannot use an approval that covers a different protocol or excluded population.

Title: Consent and notices
Acceptance intent: A participant's record identifies the exact consent materials and basis that apply.

Title: Vulnerable populations
Acceptance intent: Recruitment blocks when the required authorised consent pathway is missing.

Title: Secondary use
Acceptance intent: A deidentified dataset is rejected for a purpose excluded by its data use agreement.

Title: Participant withdrawal
Acceptance intent: The participant and study owner receive an outcome showing what ceased and what must remain.

Title: Clinical oversight
Acceptance intent: The study cannot start until a local accountable clinician accepts the oversight plan.

Title: Ethics renewal
Acceptance intent: New affected activity stops at expiry unless a valid extension is recorded.

Title: Participant communication
Acceptance intent: Messages are checked for language, confidentiality and approved content before release.

Title: Ethical complaints
Acceptance intent: A complaint receives an independent owner and cannot be deleted by the subject of the complaint.

Title: Dataset catalogue
Acceptance intent: A catalogue entry can be discoverable without exposing records or sensitive sample counts.

Title: Data access applications
Acceptance intent: The custodian can approve a restricted subset or deny with reasons.

Title: Purpose bound grants
Acceptance intent: A valid grant for evaluation cannot be used by a training job.

Title: Consent and legal basis metadata
Acceptance intent: A mixed dataset can exclude records that are not authorised for the requested purpose.

Title: Data minimisation
Acceptance intent: An evaluator using age bands cannot request dates of birth without a new approved need.

Title: Data residence
Acceptance intent: A cross border support session is evaluated under the same applicable restrictions as processing.

Title: Pseudonymisation
Acceptance intent: Evaluation users cannot recover identities using the linkage key store.

Title: Revocation and downstream impact
Acceptance intent: New access stops promptly and each affected asset receives an accountable remediation decision.

Title: Controlled exports
Acceptance intent: A result containing disallowed patient rows is withheld even when its aggregate score is releasable.

Title: Federated access
Acceptance intent: A local custodian can refuse a run or an output release independently of central scheduling.

Title: Benchmark secrecy
Acceptance intent: A developer cannot download sealed labels or bypass its submission limit with a duplicate identity.

Title: Data rights requests
Acceptance intent: A request is not automatically fulfilled in a way that destroys a lawful clinical record or legal hold.

Title: Import methods
Acceptance intent: An import without an authorised source and active access grant cannot enter a study workspace.

Title: Quarantine and scanning
Acceptance intent: A failed scan prevents previews, execution and downstream indexing.

Title: Schema and semantic validation
Acceptance intent: A plausible numeric value with an incompatible unit is flagged rather than silently accepted.

Title: Identity and deduplication
Acceptance intent: Repeated encounters remain distinguishable from accidental duplicate records.

Title: Import reconciliation
Acceptance intent: An import cannot report complete while unaccounted records remain.

Title: Resumable transfer
Acceptance intent: A resumed upload produces one verified asset with the expected checksum.

Title: Provenance lineage
Acceptance intent: A reported metric can be traced back through every material transformation.

Title: Data correction
Acceptance intent: Correcting a label creates a new dataset version and marks dependent reports for assessment.

Title: Deidentification review
Acceptance intent: Removing structured identifiers alone does not mark an imaging dataset safe to release.

Title: Scheduled ingestion
Acceptance intent: An incompatible source change pauses affected processing and identifies the responsible integration owner.

Title: Reference standard definition
Acceptance intent: A protocol cannot label an unverified model prediction as clinical ground truth.

Title: Annotation work allocation
Acceptance intent: An annotator cannot open an unassigned task or access a disallowed patient identifier.

Title: Annotation guidelines
Acceptance intent: Every label records the applicable guideline version and annotator identity.

Title: Independent labelling
Acceptance intent: Initial independent labels remain recoverable after adjudication.

Title: Agreement and quality checks
Acceptance intent: A quality report distinguishes consensus, disagreement and missing labels.

Title: Uncertain and unavailable labels
Acceptance intent: An indeterminate outcome is handled according to the prespecified analysis plan.

Title: Blinding controls
Acceptance intent: A blinded reviewer cannot see the evaluated model's prediction through exports or task history.

Title: Dataset partitions
Acceptance intent: Patient overlap across partitions is detected before an evaluation is accepted.

Title: Curation release
Acceptance intent: A released dataset cannot change its membership without a new version.

Title: Specialist annotation integrations
Acceptance intent: Imported annotations reconcile to the original task and retain reviewer attribution.

Title: Workspace request
Acceptance intent: Provisioning fails when any required grant or prerequisite is expired.

Title: Execution isolation
Acceptance intent: A workload cannot read another study's files, secrets or residual CPU or GPU memory.

Title: Network controls
Acceptance intent: A model attempting an undeclared external API call is blocked and flagged.

Title: Resource quotas
Acceptance intent: A runaway job stops at its approved limit and cannot exhaust another study's allocation.

Title: Reproducible run manifest
Acceptance intent: An authorised reviewer can reconstruct the exact configuration used for a reported result.

Title: Execution lifecycle
Acceptance intent: A failed job cannot be represented as a completed successful evaluation.

Title: Idempotent retries
Acceptance intent: A network retry creates no second charge or duplicate final result for the same logical request.

Title: External API evaluation
Acceptance intent: An unpinned provider change marks comparability uncertain and triggers review.

Title: Output handling
Acceptance intent: Logs containing patient data cannot be automatically attached to a public support ticket.

Title: Expiry and shutdown
Acceptance intent: A scheduled job cannot restart a closed workspace using an old credential.

Title: Remote execution nodes
Acceptance intent: A disconnected node cannot be assumed to have received a stop instruction.

Title: Emergency termination
Acceptance intent: Termination prevents new affected execution and records the scope, requester and observed completion status.

Title: Protocol templates
Acceptance intent: A protocol with an undefined primary endpoint cannot be frozen for formal evaluation.

Title: Study type
Acceptance intent: Study type determines required gates and allowable exposure of outputs to clinical users.

Title: Sample justification
Acceptance intent: An underpowered subgroup is labelled inconclusive rather than represented as proven safe.

Title: Prespecified thresholds
Acceptance intent: Threshold changes after results are viewed create a protocol amendment and disclosed exploratory analysis.

Title: Analysis plan
Acceptance intent: An evaluator cannot silently remove model failures from the primary denominator.

Title: Comparator definition
Acceptance intent: A comparison using different populations must disclose the limitation and cannot imply a controlled head to head result.

Title: Subgroup plan
Acceptance intent: A missing protected attribute is shown as unassessed rather than interpreted as absence of bias.

Title: Freeze and amendment
Acceptance intent: Final results link to the frozen plan and identify all departures from it.

Title: Stopping rules
Acceptance intent: A trigger crossing creates the configured hold and requires the designated independent decision.

Title: Protocol reuse
Acceptance intent: Reusing a template does not copy another country's ethics approval or clinical thresholds automatically.

Title: Risk proportional review
Acceptance intent: A high risk clinical use cannot enter through a low risk administrative template.

Title: Study registration
Acceptance intent: A claimed registered study includes a verifiable registration reference and matching scope.

Title: Task appropriate metrics
Acceptance intent: Every reported metric identifies its definition, implementation version and denominator.

Title: Diagnostic performance
Acceptance intent: Predictive values state the observed or assumed prevalence and are not transferred without qualification.

Title: Uncertainty estimates
Acceptance intent: Repeated observations from one patient are not treated as independent without justification.

Title: Calibration and utility
Acceptance intent: A high discrimination score alone cannot satisfy a protocol requiring calibration or clinical utility.

Title: Missing and rejected inputs
Acceptance intent: All attempted cases reconcile across scored, abstained, rejected and failed categories.

Title: External validation
Acceptance intent: A developer's tuning set cannot be labelled an independent external test set.

Title: Robustness testing
Acceptance intent: Reports distinguish tested conditions from unsupported assumptions about robustness.

Title: Subgroup results
Acceptance intent: A suppressed small cell remains marked as suppressed rather than displayed as zero.

Title: Baseline comparison
Acceptance intent: A benefit claim identifies both absolute and relative differences where relevant.

Title: Independent reproduction
Acceptance intent: A reproduced result outside the declared tolerance triggers an investigation before report issue.

Title: Custom metric governance
Acceptance intent: A custom metric cannot replace a primary endpoint without an approved protocol change.

Title: Evidence interpretation
Acceptance intent: A benchmark score cannot automatically issue a clinical suitability decision.

Title: Generative configuration identity
Acceptance intent: A prompt or retrieval update invalidates claims of an unchanged evaluated configuration.

Title: Clinical answer assessment
Acceptance intent: A fluent but clinically unsafe answer is treated as a safety failure under the approved rubric.

Title: Grounding and citations
Acceptance intent: A plausible fabricated citation is counted as an error rather than credited for formatting.

Title: Interaction testing
Acceptance intent: Performance reporting identifies failures that appear only across multiple turns.

Title: Language and population coverage
Acceptance intent: English performance cannot substitute for evidence in another advertised clinical language.

Title: Adversarial safety
Acceptance intent: Successful bypasses are recorded with impact and remediation evidence without releasing sensitive attack artefacts publicly.

Title: Agent permissions
Acceptance intent: A test agent cannot issue a real prescription, contact a patient or modify a live record without the separately authorised workflow.

Title: Judge validation
Acceptance intent: An unvalidated model judge cannot be the sole basis for a final clinical safety decision.

Title: Stochastic variation
Acceptance intent: Reporting one favourable run while excluding unsuccessful repetitions is prevented or explicitly disclosed.

Title: Privacy and memorisation
Acceptance intent: A model that exposes another participant's information triggers the incident and hold workflow.

Title: Cost and latency tradeoffs
Acceptance intent: A low per token price cannot be reported as total workflow cost.

Title: Synthetic evaluation limits
Acceptance intent: Passing synthetic scenarios cannot automatically satisfy a requirement for prospective clinical evidence.

Title: Tabular prediction
Acceptance intent: Post outcome variables are identified before a prediction evaluation is accepted.

Title: Imaging evaluation
Acceptance intent: Results retain linkage to the correct examination and evaluated image series.

Title: Clinical text
Acceptance intent: A summary evaluation can identify clinically material omissions from the authorised source record.

Title: Speech and audio
Acceptance intent: Medical term errors and consequential negation errors remain distinguishable from ordinary word errors.

Title: Signals and devices
Acceptance intent: Misaligned sensor timestamps cannot be silently compared to clinical event labels.

Title: Multimodal systems
Acceptance intent: A solution's advertised fallback behaviour is tested when one required modality is absent.

Title: Administrative and public health AI
Acceptance intent: A scheduling model is not assigned diagnostic metrics solely because it operates in a hospital.

Title: Capability admission
Acceptance intent: Unsupported tasks remain in discovery status and cannot receive a formal validated result.

Title: Workflow definition
Acceptance intent: A model result cannot be interpreted without its intended position in the clinical workflow.

Title: Usability studies
Acceptance intent: A usability report identifies participant roles and includes observed failures as well as satisfaction.

Title: Human AI interaction
Acceptance intent: An apparent time saving is qualified when required verification work is omitted.

Title: Accessibility and inclusion
Acceptance intent: A deployment plan includes mitigations for material exclusion risks identified during evaluation.

Title: Clinical workflow outcomes
Acceptance intent: A high detection rate alone cannot establish benefit when the protocol requires completed referral.

Title: Training effectiveness
Acceptance intent: An untrained user cannot be enabled for a function requiring verified competence.

Title: Equity interpretation
Acceptance intent: The report identifies who may lose access or bear additional costs under the proposed workflow.

Title: Patient and staff feedback
Acceptance intent: Negative feedback remains visible to reviewers even when a site or developer disputes it.

Title: Economic measurement
Acceptance intent: A cost effectiveness calculation states perspective, currency, price year, assumptions and uncertainty.

Title: Site activation
Acceptance intent: No recruitment or care affecting evaluation can begin at an inactive site.

Title: Eligibility and enrolment
Acceptance intent: An ineligible enrolment creates a deviation and cannot be silently corrected out of the record.

Title: Participant identifiers
Acceptance intent: Central evaluators receive only the participant information authorised by their study role.

Title: Case report forms
Acceptance intent: A corrected clinical observation retains its original value, reason, actor and timestamp.

Title: Allocation and blinding
Acceptance intent: Only authorised staff can unblind, with reason and downstream impact recorded.

Title: Silent prospective mode
Acceptance intent: A silent mode prediction cannot appear in a clinician's production worklist.

Title: Interventional controls
Acceptance intent: A changed clinical configuration requires the defined amendment process before use.

Title: Deviations and queries
Acceptance intent: A deviation affecting participant safety triggers escalation independently of ordinary data cleaning.

Title: Monitoring and verification
Acceptance intent: Monitoring findings have accountable corrective actions and verifiable closure evidence.

Title: Safety reporting
Acceptance intent: A report initiates safety review without waiting for causality to be proven.

Title: Study closeout
Acceptance intent: A study cannot be marked fully closed while mandatory follow up obligations remain unassigned.

Title: External study systems
Acceptance intent: An imported record retains source identity and does not create an inconsistent competing master record.

Title: Safety case
Acceptance intent: No clinical use proceeds with an unaccepted material residual risk.

Title: Incident intake
Acceptance intent: A reporter can raise a concern without needing permission from the implicated developer.

Title: Severity and triage
Acceptance intent: An incomplete but potentially serious report enters urgent review rather than being rejected by form validation.

Title: Containment
Acceptance intent: A targeted suspension prevents affected new activity without concealing historical evidence.

Title: Deployment stop coordination
Acceptance intent: An unacknowledged instruction remains visibly unresolved and escalates to local contacts.

Title: Investigation
Acceptance intent: An implicated party cannot alter retained evidence or close its own independent investigation.

Title: Corrective and preventive action
Acceptance intent: Closing an action requires verification evidence rather than a completion checkbox alone.

Title: Reportability assessment
Acceptance intent: The platform records proof of submission or an explicit failure; an internal alert is not treated as statutory reporting.

Title: Cross study impact
Acceptance intent: A recalled model component produces an actionable list of impacted evaluations and deployments.

Title: Resumption decision
Acceptance intent: Commercial pressure or payment status cannot override an active safety hold.

Title: External warning exchange
Acceptance intent: A shared warning excludes unauthorised patient data and clearly states unresolved causality.

Title: Learning and trend review
Acceptance intent: Repeated low severity incidents can trigger a systemic risk review.

Title: Evidence dossier
Acceptance intent: A reviewer can trace each headline finding to the underlying approved evidence.

Title: Claim level provenance
Acceptance intent: A new product version does not inherit an unsupported claim from an earlier version.

Title: Evidence status
Acceptance intent: Insufficient evidence cannot be displayed as a positive outcome or averaged into a pass.

Title: Independent review
Acceptance intent: A developer response is retained but cannot replace the independent conclusion.

Title: Report generation
Acceptance intent: Regenerated reports preserve the same approved findings and identify the generator version.

Title: Scope and limitations
Acceptance intent: A report cannot omit a material failed subgroup that was included in the approved analysis plan.

Title: Publication permissions
Acceptance intent: A public report does not reveal protected small cells, patient details or proprietary artefacts.

Title: Signed release and integrity
Acceptance intent: Altering a released report creates a new version and invalidates the altered copy's integrity check.

Title: Corrections and retractions
Acceptance intent: Opening a superseded report displays its current status and link to the authoritative successor.

Title: Evidence portability
Acceptance intent: A receiving institution can identify what may be reused and what needs local validation.

Title: Results completeness
Acceptance intent: Unreported endpoints block issue or require an explicit approved explanation.

Title: Public evidence catalogue
Acceptance intent: Catalogue presence is not presented as an endorsement or universal approval.

Title: Requirements checklist
Acceptance intent: Each required item identifies its evidence location or a documented gap.

Title: Submission packages
Acceptance intent: A package can contain different evidence and forms for two jurisdictions without changing the underlying findings.

Title: External decision verification
Acceptance intent: A developer assertion remains unverified until the designated verification process completes.

Title: Authority questions
Acceptance intent: A response can be linked to the exact question and submitted file version.

Title: Decision separation
Acceptance intent: Completing an internal checklist cannot mark a product legally authorised.

Title: Change submissions
Acceptance intent: A changed intended use triggers a regulatory impact task before clinical continuation.

Title: Permission expiry
Acceptance intent: A withdrawn permission blocks affected new activity and initiates impact review.

Title: Submission channel control
Acceptance intent: Preparing a package never automatically transmits it to an authority.

Title: Transfer request
Acceptance intent: The request references a specific product and dossier version.

Title: Gap assessment
Acceptance intent: The assessment identifies evidence that is reusable, uncertain or inapplicable with reasons.

Title: Local validation plan
Acceptance intent: A foreign positive report cannot bypass an unresolved local safety or applicability requirement.

Title: Adaptation tracking
Acceptance intent: Local modifications remain distinguishable from the original evaluated product.

Title: Evidence reliance decisions
Acceptance intent: No automated evidence passport grants mutual recognition between countries.

Title: Shared studies
Acceptance intent: A pooled result preserves country level findings and cannot conceal a material local failure.

Title: Reuse measurement
Acceptance intent: Estimated savings remain labelled estimates and do not double count shared work.

Title: Country withdrawal
Acceptance intent: Withdrawal blocks new sharing without erasing lawful historical evidence or incident responsibilities.

Title: Adoption readiness
Acceptance intent: A scientifically successful evaluation can remain operationally unready with explicit blockers.

Title: Business case
Acceptance intent: The case includes integration and recurring operating costs as well as licence fees.

Title: Procurement support
Acceptance intent: Paid participation cannot silently change procurement ranking or evaluation criteria.

Title: Deployment authorisation
Acceptance intent: A sandbox completion status alone cannot authorise production deployment.

Title: Implementation plan
Acceptance intent: Go live requires evidence that applicable readiness tasks are complete.

Title: Acceptance and fallback
Acceptance intent: A failed integration acceptance test blocks the affected go live.

Title: Training and competency
Acceptance intent: A user can be restricted from a clinical feature after required training expires.

Title: Production boundary
Acceptance intent: An evaluation credential cannot write to a production patient record.

Title: Contract and budget transition
Acceptance intent: A pilot nearing funding expiry shows an accountable continuation or closure decision.

Title: Deployment register
Acceptance intent: A recall can locate all registered deployments of an affected version.

Title: Benefits realisation
Acceptance intent: An adoption report identifies baseline, attribution limits and incomplete follow up.

Title: Safe termination
Acceptance intent: A vendor exit leaves the institution with a documented transition and retained lawful records.

Title: Monitoring plan
Acceptance intent: A deployment cannot be labelled monitored without an active plan and functioning data source.

Title: Operational telemetry
Acceptance intent: A missing telemetry feed is reported as unavailable rather than interpreted as zero incidents.

Title: Clinical performance follow up
Acceptance intent: Recent unlabelled cases cannot be counted as successful outcomes.

Title: Drift detection
Acceptance intent: A statistical drift signal creates a review rather than an unsupported conclusion of patient harm.

Title: Version change intake
Acceptance intent: A changed component identifies the associated evidence and monitoring plans for reassessment.

Title: Change classification
Acceptance intent: A developer cannot unilaterally declare a material clinical change insignificant.

Title: Revalidation scheduling
Acceptance intent: An overdue required revalidation produces an explicit restricted or expired evidence status.

Title: Alert routing
Acceptance intent: Unacknowledged urgent alerts reach the backup contact within the configured escalation period.

Title: Rollback tracking
Acceptance intent: Central issuance does not imply a site completed rollback without positive confirmation.

Title: Comparative surveillance
Acceptance intent: A dashboard discloses incomparable denominators and cannot imply a global product ranking.

Title: Monitoring handover
Acceptance intent: No deployment remains represented as actively monitored after its responsible service has stopped.

Title: Evidence freshness
Acceptance intent: A buyer can identify that installed software differs from the version supporting a published claim.

Title: Role specific dashboards
Acceptance intent: A funder sees approved programme outcomes without receiving patient records by default.

Title: Portfolio funnel
Acceptance intent: A failed scientific evaluation is distinguishable from an unfunded otherwise suitable solution.

Title: Time and bottlenecks
Acceptance intent: Reported turnaround includes a published rule for paused and abandoned studies.

Title: Evidence quality reporting
Acceptance intent: A large number of tests cannot substitute for missing independent clinical validation.

Title: Outcome reporting
Acceptance intent: Patient reach is not displayed as demonstrated health benefit.

Title: Resource and financial reporting
Acceptance intent: Study cost reconciles with approved compute, personnel and external service charges.

Title: Governed metrics
Acceptance intent: A changed definition is visible in longitudinal comparisons.

Title: Privacy preserving reporting
Acceptance intent: Repeated small group queries cannot trivially reconstruct a protected individual's result.

Title: Report exports
Acceptance intent: An exported chart retains qualifications that materially affect its interpretation.

Title: Scheduled reporting
Acceptance intent: A recipient removed before delivery does not receive the scheduled restricted report.

Title: Contextual discussions
Acceptance intent: A comment mentioning a restricted study does not expose it to an unauthorised tagged user.

Title: Assignments and reminders
Acceptance intent: A task cannot disappear when its assigned user leaves the organisation.

Title: Notifications
Acceptance intent: Email subject lines and push previews do not include patient identifiers or confidential findings.

Title: Consequential communications
Acceptance intent: Drafting a message or report does not send or publish it automatically.

Title: Meeting decisions
Acceptance intent: A discussion summary cannot silently substitute for a required formal gate decision.

Title: Document collaboration
Acceptance intent: One reviewer's edit cannot overwrite another reviewer's change without resolution.

Title: Translation review
Acceptance intent: An unreviewed machine translation is marked draft and cannot serve as approved consent material.

Title: Communication audit
Acceptance intent: A failed delivery is not counted as successful notification.

Title: Knowledge library
Acceptance intent: Outdated guidance is labelled and excluded from default new study templates.

Title: Learning from failure
Acceptance intent: A case study can describe failure without exposing a protected developer or participant.

Title: Role based onboarding
Acceptance intent: Completion of mandatory onboarding is checked before restricted access is activated.

Title: Training records
Acceptance intent: Changing a material procedure identifies users requiring refresher training.

Title: Community exchange
Acceptance intent: A community post cannot reveal sealed test data or private review materials.

Title: Method governance
Acceptance intent: An experimental metric remains clearly identified until its review is complete.

Title: Network learning reports
Acceptance intent: Published lessons distinguish observed findings from hypotheses and cannot imply universal applicability.

Title: Assisted drafting
Acceptance intent: Drafts are labelled as AI assisted and cannot become signed decisions without human review.

Title: Permission aware retrieval
Acceptance intent: A prompt cannot expose another tenant's document, hidden review or sealed benchmark.

Title: Source attribution
Acceptance intent: Unsupported findings are flagged and are not inserted as verified study results.

Title: Consequential action control
Acceptance intent: Every consequential action requires the specified authorised human confirmation and gate checks.

Title: Provider governance
Acceptance intent: Restricted study content is not sent to a provider lacking applicable approval.

Title: Untrusted content handling
Acceptance intent: Embedded instructions in a document cannot trigger an export or disable a review gate.

Title: User correction
Acceptance intent: Correcting a draft does not erase the fact that AI assistance was used.

Title: Assistant evaluation
Acceptance intent: A failed critical safety or permission test prevents release of the feature.

Title: Administrative controls
Acceptance intent: A disabled feature cannot be invoked through an API or background task.

Title: Fallback and abstention
Acceptance intent: A failed AI service cannot prevent an authorised user from filing a safety incident.

Title: Versioned interfaces
Acceptance intent: A published integration can identify the API version and supported deprecation period.

Title: Scoped integration access
Acceptance intent: A reporting connector cannot inherit permission to export raw clinical data.

Title: Health record exchange
Acceptance intent: Profile validation and unit or terminology mapping pass agreed conformance examples before activation.

Title: Medical imaging exchange
Acceptance intent: Transferred images retain clinically necessary metadata while prohibited identifiers are handled as approved.

Title: Research and health information systems
Acceptance intent: Each connected field has an identified authoritative source and reconciliation rule.

Title: Import and export portability
Acceptance intent: A receiving tool can reconstruct object relationships from an approved export.

Title: Reliable events
Acceptance intent: Repeated delivery does not duplicate a clinical decision, invoice or approval.

Title: Connector failures
Acceptance intent: An unavailable external system cannot cause silent loss of an acknowledged source record.

Title: Mapping governance
Acceptance intent: An unrecognised clinical code is quarantined or explicitly represented rather than silently replaced.

Title: Identity and finance integrations
Acceptance intent: An accounting integration receives billing data without gaining clinical evidence access.

Title: Connector lifecycle
Acceptance intent: Disabling a connector stops new transfers and preserves the record of past exchanges.

Title: External evidence exchange
Acceptance intent: An external directory receives only the authorised metadata and current evidence status.

Title: Service catalogue
Acceptance intent: A buyer can identify which activities and deliverables are included before contracting.

Title: Cost estimation
Acceptance intent: Estimate changes identify the driver and require the applicable budget approval.

Title: Quotes and approvals
Acceptance intent: A change in scope cannot silently increase an institution's financial commitment.

Title: Budget controls
Acceptance intent: A study cannot exceed its approved hard spending limit through automatic retries.

Title: Usage metering
Acceptance intent: A failed retry is charged only according to the declared billing policy.

Title: Invoices and payments
Acceptance intent: An issued credit links to the original invoice and preserves audit history.

Title: Grant and subsidy management
Acceptance intent: A subsidised evaluation shows the payer without changing the scientific scoring rules.

Title: Commercial independence
Acceptance intent: An overdue invoice cannot delete unfavourable evidence or prevent an urgent safety report.

Title: Financial disputes
Acceptance intent: A scientific appeal remains available under its own policy despite an unrelated invoice dispute.

Title: Renewal and exit
Acceptance intent: Service expiry triggers a documented handover and removes unsupported active monitoring claims.

Title: Audit coverage
Acceptance intent: A sampled sensitive action can be traced to actor, scope, object version, time and outcome.

Title: Audit integrity
Acceptance intent: An administrator cannot alter an event without detection and a separately retained record.

Title: Before and after changes
Acceptance intent: An investigator can reconstruct a permission change without exposing authentication credentials.

Title: Audit access
Acceptance intent: An auditor cannot approve the report being audited.

Title: Control evidence library
Acceptance intent: A requested control can be linked to its latest verification and unresolved findings.

Title: Compliance mapping
Acceptance intent: The platform cannot advertise compliance solely because a checklist template exists.

Title: Inspection support
Acceptance intent: The exported inspection package reconciles to the selected source versions.

Title: Legal holds
Acceptance intent: A scheduled deletion cannot remove a held record or its required supporting evidence.

Title: Exceptions and expiry
Acceptance intent: An expired exception cannot silently remain active.

Title: Periodic assurance review
Acceptance intent: A recurring critical finding triggers escalation to the appropriate governance body.

Title: Certification claims
Acceptance intent: An assessment in progress is never displayed as a completed certification.

Title: Audit retention
Acceptance intent: Audit logs cannot be retained indefinitely solely because storage is available.

Title: Operational console
Acceptance intent: Support can identify a failed job using metadata and approved diagnostics.

Title: Support access
Acceptance intent: A user filing a ticket does not grant blanket access to all institutional data.

Title: Incident management
Acceptance intent: Major incidents preserve a timeline and tracked corrective actions.

Title: Configuration control
Acceptance intent: Changing an access rule records who approved it and what affected scopes were assessed.

Title: Feature activation
Acceptance intent: Enabling a user interface feature cannot bypass a missing clinical capability approval.

Title: Service notices
Acceptance intent: Users can distinguish a planned outage from failure of their own study.

Title: Capacity and quota management
Acceptance intent: A large commercial customer cannot consume protected capacity assigned to an active safety investigation.

Title: Backup and restore operations
Acceptance intent: A restored environment does not reactivate revoked users or deleted data without reconciliation.

Title: Release management
Acceptance intent: A metric implementation update cannot silently alter previously issued results.

Title: Support service catalogue
Acceptance intent: Clinical sites have a local urgent route even when ordinary technical support is unavailable.

Title: Supplier continuity
Acceptance intent: A supplier outage can be linked to affected studies and recovery options.

Title: Institutional service reviews
Acceptance intent: Actions from the review have owners and due dates visible to both parties.

Title: Retention schedules
Acceptance intent: A newly created asset inherits an explicit retention policy rather than an indefinite default.

Title: Study closure
Acceptance intent: A study cannot close its safety obligations by changing its administrative status.

Title: Data disposal
Acceptance intent: A disposal record identifies completed actions, retained exceptions and backup expiry treatment.

Title: Backup deletion handling
Acceptance intent: A restore applies the current deletion and revocation ledger before user access resumes.

Title: Institutional export
Acceptance intent: An export includes relationship keys and definitions needed to interpret the files.

Title: Rights aware portability
Acceptance intent: A departing partner cannot take another institution's raw data merely because both joined a study.

Title: User and tenant offboarding
Acceptance intent: Deleting a user profile does not destroy the attribution of a clinical signoff.

Title: Operator succession
Acceptance intent: A tabletop exercise identifies who would receive evidence and incident responsibilities.

Title: Closure attestation
Acceptance intent: An attestation never claims deletion of data still retained under a documented hold.

Title: Residual obligations
Acceptance intent: An expired commercial agreement does not remove a required safety follow up task.

Title: Security verification baseline
Acceptance intent: An independent assessment records applicability and evidence; no unresolved exploitable critical or high finding remains at launch.

Title: Transport protection
Acceptance intent: Scanning finds no accepted plaintext protected endpoint or obsolete protocol; certificate failure blocks connection.

Title: Stored data protection
Acceptance intent: Storage and backup inspection finds no unencrypted restricted payload or plaintext secret.

Title: Authentication coverage
Acceptance intent: Attempts to enter these scopes without the required assurance are denied in all supported clients.

Title: Local credential policy
Acceptance intent: Password managers and paste work; recovery and change tests invalidate compromised sessions as specified.

Title: Session expiry
Acceptance intent: Boundary tests confirm expiry and step up checks without losing safely saved drafts.

Title: Revocation latency
Acceptance intent: A distributed revocation test has no successful new protected action after the deadline; offline limits are documented separately.

Title: Isolation assurance
Acceptance intent: No unauthorised access succeeds in the release suite or independent penetration test.

Title: Secret handling
Acceptance intent: Automated scans and sampled runtime inspection find no exposed active secret; rotation does not broaden access.

Title: Abuse protection
Acceptance intent: Load and brute force tests are contained without preventing the approved emergency reporting route.

Title: Vulnerability response
Acceptance intent: The vulnerability register measures discovery to containment and remediation, with overdue escalation.

Title: Independent testing
Acceptance intent: Evidence includes remediation and retest of affected controls rather than only the original report.

Title: Residency coverage
Acceptance intent: A residency inventory and technical validation show no unapproved processing or copy location.

Title: Purpose enforcement
Acceptance intent: A sampled audit and negative tests find no run or export without the required grant.

Title: Minimised telemetry
Acceptance intent: Synthetic sensitive markers inserted into test workflows do not appear in general telemetry.

Title: Disclosure control
Acceptance intent: A disclosure test pack verifies suppression and complementary cell handling for all supported filters and exports.

Title: Privacy impact review
Acceptance intent: A release cannot enable the affected processing while a mandatory assessment is incomplete.

Title: Data rights service
Acceptance intent: The case register tracks deadlines, identity checks, holds and reasoned outcomes without assuming one global deadline.

Title: Deletion execution
Acceptance intent: Verification confirms active deletion and prevents restoration from reintroducing disposed records.

Title: Provider data use
Acceptance intent: Provider configuration and terms are verified before use; an unapproved change stops affected transmission.

Title: Core availability
Acceptance intent: Independent probes and incident records reconcile successful available minutes; third party failures affecting the journey count.

Title: Emergency reporting continuity
Acceptance intent: A quarterly outage exercise reaches an accountable operator and the relevant local site contact.

Title: Recovery time
Acceptance intent: A twice yearly recovery exercise meets the target within permitted residency locations.

Title: Recovery point
Acceptance intent: A recovery test demonstrates bounded loss and reconciles any missing authoritative actions before reopening access.

Title: Source data recovery
Acceptance intent: Restored inputs reconcile to the frozen manifest; a missing unique input blocks dependent evidence claims.

Title: Backup verification
Acceptance intent: A completed backup job without successful restore evidence is not reported as proven recoverability.

Title: Failure isolation
Acceptance intent: Injected workload and dependency failures leave unrelated critical journeys functional.

Title: Safe degraded operation
Acceptance intent: Dependency failure cannot cause unrestricted access, silent approval or fabricated successful results.

Title: Disconnected sites
Acceptance intent: An offline node is never displayed as stopped or updated without evidence; its local owner receives the escalation.

Title: Interactive navigation
Acceptance intent: A 60 minute representative load test covers login landing, study list, task queue and record view.

Title: Transactional response
Acceptance intent: Measured server response includes authentication and policy checks; error rate is below 0.5 percent excluding valid client errors.

Title: Search response
Acceptance intent: The test includes complex filters and confirms that faster results do not omit access controls.

Title: Dashboard response
Acceptance intent: Heavy custom analyses are asynchronous with progress rather than blocking the application.

Title: Large ingestion
Acceptance intent: Results account for every input row; imaging and custom transforms use separately approved budgets.

Title: Queue responsiveness
Acceptance intent: Queue metrics distinguish unavailable resources, policy holds and scheduler delay.

Title: Large exports
Acceptance intent: The user sees progress and expiry; authorisation is rechecked before download.

Title: Low bandwidth use
Acceptance intent: Users can save an application, review a task and report an incident under the constrained profile.

Title: Inference budgets
Acceptance intent: Out of budget runs terminate or queue according to policy with clear evidence and billing treatment.

Title: Capacity expansion
Acceptance intent: Capacity approval is supported by load test evidence and estimated operating cost.

Title: Acknowledged transactions
Acceptance intent: Failure injection yields either one complete recorded action or an explicit failure, never a partial approval.

Title: Artefact integrity
Acceptance intent: Changing bytes changes the integrity result and cannot preserve the original verified status.

Title: Provenance completeness
Acceptance intent: An automated completeness check blocks formal issue when any required link is missing.

Title: Deterministic reproducibility
Acceptance intent: Results outside tolerance are investigated and cannot be released as reproduced.

Title: Stochastic reproducibility
Acceptance intent: A result's reproducibility statement does not promise identical output from a nondeterministic external model.

Title: Clock consistency
Acceptance intent: A trace reconstruction preserves event order; unsynchronised external timestamps are explicitly identified.

Title: Numerical semantics
Acceptance intent: Round trip tests preserve each state and do not convert missing clinical values to zero.

Title: Concurrent edits
Acceptance intent: Two simultaneous protocol edits produce an explicit conflict or preserved merge history.

Title: Accessibility baseline
Acceptance intent: Automated checks plus manual keyboard, screen reader, focus and zoom testing find no unresolved critical barrier.

Title: Task success
Acceptance intent: Usability sessions include at least 5 participants per priority role and document failures and remediation.

Title: Navigation and status clarity
Acceptance intent: Users correctly identify the next action in at least 90 percent of sampled task scenarios.

Title: Error prevention
Acceptance intent: Tests prevent accidental publication, deletion and role escalation through one unintended ordinary click.

Title: Responsive support
Acceptance intent: Testing at agreed mobile and desktop sizes finds no blocked critical workflow or inaccessible control.

Title: Browser support
Acceptance intent: The release matrix records tested versions and known limitations; specialised viewers declare separate support.

Title: Language readiness
Acceptance intent: Pseudo localisation does not clip critical controls or corrupt exported clinical terminology.

Title: Translation integrity
Acceptance intent: Unapproved translations cannot appear as final participant or authority documents.

Title: Assisted accessibility
Acceptance intent: A user unable to use the primary media format can complete the same required training outcome.

Title: Critical monitoring
Acceptance intent: A controlled critical failure generates an operational alert within 5 minutes.

Title: Incident acknowledgement
Acceptance intent: Quarterly drills demonstrate contactability and backup escalation; ordinary support hours are separately published.

Title: User communications
Acceptance intent: The communication log records delivery failures and contains no unauthorised sensitive data.

Title: Traceability
Acceptance intent: An incident investigation can connect the initiating request with all material outcomes.

Title: Operational history
Acceptance intent: Operators can investigate a sampled 60 day old incident without accessing raw patient data.

Title: Runbook coverage
Acceptance intent: A new on call operator can execute sampled runbooks during a supervised readiness exercise.

Title: Post incident review
Acceptance intent: Repeat causes and overdue actions appear in the service governance review.

Title: Release traceability
Acceptance intent: A sampled release can be traced to its business reason and rollback or recovery plan.

Title: Regression gates
Acceptance intent: A failing critical permission, safety, provenance or metric test blocks deployment.

Title: Rollback readiness
Acceptance intent: A rehearsal restores service without discarding acknowledged records or reviving revoked access.

Title: Migration assurance
Acceptance intent: A failed reconciliation prevents the migrated environment from serving affected production records.

Title: Interface stability
Acceptance intent: A breaking change cannot silently invalidate an agreed institutional connector.

Title: Dependency governance
Acceptance intent: Unsupported critical dependencies have a funded replacement or approved time limited exception.

Title: Portability
Acceptance intent: A clean environment reconstructs a sampled exported study and verifies its evidence references.

Title: Environment flexibility
Acceptance intent: Each offered profile passes equivalent access, provenance, safety and operational gates before sale.

Title: No universal clinical score
Acceptance intent: An undefined threshold or unsupported population blocks a suitability conclusion.

Title: Platform assistant safety
Acceptance intent: The report discloses sample size and residual uncertainty; zero observed failures is not claimed as zero real world risk.

Title: Generated factual grounding
Acceptance intent: A random audit of released reports finds no unreviewed material generated claim.

Title: Model change regression
Acceptance intent: Changes cannot enter production based solely on improved average response quality.

Title: Human review independence
Acceptance intent: Workflow tests require the appropriate eligible human decision for each protected outcome.

Title: AI service continuity
Acceptance intent: A simulated provider outage leaves manual authorised completion possible without data loss.

Title: Cost attribution
Acceptance intent: Monthly financial reconciliation explains the remaining unattributed amount.

Title: Spending limits
Acceptance intent: The hard limit prevents further unauthorised spending while preserving evidence and safe termination.

Title: Idle resource control
Acceptance intent: An idle workspace stops compute charges without deleting retained assets or disrupting a declared long job.

Title: Resource reporting
Acceptance intent: Estimates do not imply measured carbon emissions when only proxy data are available.

Title: Operational ownership
Acceptance intent: No feature is released with an unassigned safety or maintenance responsibility.

Title: Documentation completeness
Acceptance intent: Representative users complete the documented core journeys without undocumented internal assistance.

Title: Country launch readiness
Acceptance intent: A country cannot be marked active through marketing configuration alone.

Title: Service request response
Acceptance intent: Reports measure compliance from receipt and distinguish acknowledgement from resolution.

Title: Continuity responsibilities
Acceptance intent: A tabletop exercise shows safe local action during a platform or network outage.

Title: Exit readiness
Acceptance intent: The exercise records gaps, assigned remedies and lawful retained obligations.
